title: The rice field
text:
In planting time, the field's a mirror,
Holding the clouds and the morning sun.
Farmers wade in with their trousers rolled,
Pressing in seedlings, one by one.

White egrets step on their long, thin legs,
Hunting for snails in the shallow pool,
While children wave from the narrow path
As they hurry along on their way to school.

Soon the seedlings grow into a carpet,
Rippling and swaying when the breezes blow.
Frogs sing loudly as night time gathers,
A croaking choir in the mud below.

By harvest time, the green has faded.
The stalks hang heavy, bending low,
And all the field is as gold as honey,
Shining bright in the sunset's glow.

Tin cans rattle on strings and poles
To keep the hungry sparrows from the grain.
The birds fly up in a chattering cloud,
Then sneak back down to try again.

Then come the sickles, swish, swish, swish,
And bundles stacked in a golden pile.
The grain is spread on woven mats to dry
Under the sun for a little while.

At last the field lies bare and quiet,
Resting under the soft, grey rain,
Dreaming of the next planting season,
When it will be a mirror again.
